subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should trusted in-process plugin-runtime callers be restricted to `sessions.patch` only when the persisted row's `pluginOwnerId` exactly matches, with ownerless rows rejected?
rationale: The rule aligns patch with the existing delete fence and closes cross-plugin mutation, but it deliberately removes trusted-plugin access to ordinary ownerless sessions and therefore needs an explicit authorization-boundary decision.

options.title: Require exact ownership
options.body: Reject foreign and ownerless rows, while allowing plugin-created rows after the pre-migration authorization defect and deployed proof are addressed.

options.title: Add a privileged bypass
options.body: Define a separate explicit trusted capability for plugins that must patch operator-owned or ownerless sessions instead of weakening the default ownership fence.

options.title: Pause both candidates
options.body: Keep the issue and both PRs open until the permanent trusted-plugin session authority model is decided.

recommendation.title: Require exact ownership
recommendation.body: Reject foreign and ownerless rows, while allowing plugin-created rows after the pre-migration authorization defect and deployed proof are addressed.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter introduced the current ownership field, creation stamping, and sibling delete fence that establish the policy being extended.
